$S_1\in \mathbb{C}^{q\times q}$ with $\det S_1\ne 0$, $S_2\in \mathbb{C}^{q\times q}$,

By applying Theorem~\ref{th3.2} with
$S_1^{-1}={\Lambda}_{R,1}$, $U_1=X^\top=T_{R,1}$,  $S_2={\Lambda}_{G,1}$, $V_2=Y^\top=W_{G,1}$, we find

issues.failure_explanation: The left factor $(I_m+zX(S_1-zI_q)^{-1}U_1)$ of $\widetilde A(z)$ has poles at the eigenvalues of $S_1$; for $\widetilde A(z)$ to be a quadratic matrix polynomial these poles must be canceled by zeros of $A(z)$, which is encoded by the left-evaluation condition $U_1A_0 + S_1U_1A_1 + S_1^2U_1A_2 = 0$ (equivalently $S_1^{-2}U_1A_0+S_1^{-1}U_1A_1+U_1A_2=0$). The displayed hypothesis instead pairs $S_1^2$ with $A_0$ and $S_1$ with $A_1$, and its last term $S_2A_2$ is a product of a $q\times q$ matrix with an $m\times m$ matrix, which is undefined for $1\le q<m$. With the hypothesis as printed the conclusion does not follow and generically fails ($\widetilde A$ keeps poles at $\sigma(S_1)$); moreover Section 3 invokes the theorem with $S_1^{-1}=\Lambda_{R,1}$ and can only verify the corrected relation $\Lambda_{R,1}^2T_{R,1}A_0+\Lambda_{R,1}T_{R,1}A_1+T_{R,1}A_2=0$ of \eqref{10}, so the invocation does not meet the stated hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first displayed hypothesis of Theorem th3.2 by $U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0$ (equivalently $S_1^{-2}U_1A_0+S_1^{-1}U_1A_1+U_1A_2=0$); this is precisely the relation the paper's Section 3 establishes in \eqref{10}, so all downstream claims are restored without further changes.
issues.overall_effect: The deflation construction of Section 3 (coefficients of $\widetilde A$, the $\bar A_i$ of (19)-(21), the reduced QMEs \eqref{eq:qmeGbar}/\eqref{eq:qmeRbar}, and the justification of Algorithms alg:isg/alg:gfull) loses its cited support; all of it is restored once the hypothesis is corrected, since the corrected condition is exactly the one verified in \eqref{10}.
issues.title: First hypothesis of the block shift-and-deflate theorem (th3.2) is undefined and is not the condition its conclusion needs
issues.why_classification: A single locally forced display correction (determined by the paper's own \eqref{10} and Theorem th5) repairs the theorem, its dependents, and the algorithmic pipeline; no substantive claim, rate, or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers the nullity limit from 'as $k\to\infty$, $a_k(z)$ has exactly $m-\ell$ zeros that converge to 0'. Roots tending to 0 do not make the matrices singular: under the proof's own assumptions (no breakdown, $\det A_1^{(k)}\ne0$), $A_{0}^{(k+1)}=A_{0}^{(k)}(A_{1}^{(k)})^{-1}A_{0}^{(k)}$ is a product of nonsingular matrices, so if $A_0$ is nonsingular every $A_0^{(k)}$ (and $A_2^{(k)}$) stays nonsingular and all nullities are 0 while $m-\ell\ge1$. The paper's own Example 3 is such a case: $A_0=PG$ with $P$ nonsingular and $G$ nonsingular, so the stated limit fails on an admissible instance. Hence the proposition's final claim is false as stated, and the identification of span$(V_{0,2}^{(k)})$ (resp. rows of $U_{2,2}^{(k)}$) with the invariant subspace of $G$ (resp. $R$) — equation (10-1), the formulas for $S_G$, $S_R$, and the guarantee of Algorithm alg:isg — is asserted without the required singular-subspace convergence argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false nullity statement by the (supported) statement that the $m-\ell$ smallest singular values of $A_0^{(k)}$ and $A_2^{(k)}$ tend to 0, and supply a genuine proof that the trailing singular subspaces converge to the invariant subspaces of $G$ and $R$ (e.g., via a singular-value gap derived from \eqref{eq:roots_separation}); the limsup bounds already proven remain valid.
issues.overall_effect: The final claim of Proposition prop:A0KW is false; the paper's central mechanism — extracting $W_{G,1},\Lambda_{G,1},T_{R,1},\Lambda_{R,1}$ from SVDs of the CR iterates (Algorithm alg:isg, used by alg:gfull) — is left without valid support.
issues.title: Proposition prop:A0KW asserts lim nullity(A_i^{(k)}) = m−ℓ, which is false
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new contained argument (singular-subspace convergence under the spectral gap) that the source does not contain, but no new global architecture is needed and the paper's results, rates, and guarantees all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$$
Q^* M Z=T, \quad Q^* N Z=S
$$
with $Q$ and $Z$ unitary and $T$ and $S$ upper triangular

issues.failure_explanation: From $Q^*MZ=T$ and $Q^*NZ=S$ with $T,S$ upper block triangular, the first $\ell$ columns satisfy $MZ_{\cdot 1}=Q\,T_{\cdot 1}=Q[\,T_{11};\,0\,]$ and $NZ_{\cdot 1}=Q[\,S_{11};\,0\,]$, hence $MZ_{\cdot 1}=NZ_{\cdot 1}(S_{11}^{-1}T_{11})$; combining with Lemma lem:added-1 and $Z_{\cdot 1}=[\,I;\,\bar G_{11}\,]Z_{11}$ gives $\bar G_{11}=Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1}=Z_{11}(S_{11}^{-1}T_{11})Z_{11}^{-1}$. The claimed equality with $Q_{11}T_{11}S_{11}^{-1}Q_{11}^{-1}$ uses the left Schur vectors $Q$ instead of $Z$ and the reversed product order; for $\ell\ge2$ neither replacement is valid in general ($Q_{11}\neq Z_{11}$, and $T_{11}S_{11}^{-1}\ne S_{11}^{-1}T_{11}$ generically), so the algorithm as written returns a matrix with the correct eigenvalues but that is not the solution of \eqref{eq:qmeB}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false second equality (the formula $\bar G_{11}=Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1}$ already delivers the stated output), or replace it by the correct identity $\bar G_{11}=Z_{11}S_{11}^{-1}T_{11}Z_{11}^{-1}$.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:QZ's stated computation does not deliver its stated output (the solution $\bar G_{11}$ with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$); Algorithm alg:gfull, which calls it, inherits the wrong value of $\bar G_{11}$ and hence of $G$ and $R$.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:QZ's second extraction formula is a false identity
issues.why_classification: A one-line local deletion/correction of an identity restores the stated input-output guarantee; no other step or claim is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, from the numerical experiments, the proposed approach is much more accurate than classical CR.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims BS-CR is the most accurate method; the paper's own Table tab:example1 for Example 1 reports residual $3.9\cdot10^{-15}$ for BS-CR versus $4.4\cdot10^{-16}$ for CR, i.e., classical CR is about nine times more accurate there. The Introduction's blanket statement that the proposed approach is 'much more accurate than classical CR' is likewise contradicted by Example 1; the experiments support only that BS-CR is far more accurate in Examples 2–3 and comparable in Example 1.

failure_location.quote: Concerning residual error, \texttt{BS-CR} is clearly the most accurate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the accuracy statements (e.g., 'BS-CR is the most accurate in Examples 2 and 3 and comparable to CR in Example 1').
issues.overall_effect: The experimental-summary claims (Introduction and Section 7.1) materially overstate what the experiments show; no formal result or algorithm guarantee is affected.
issues.title: Accuracy of BS-CR overclaimed against the paper's own Example 1
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of a prose summary fixes it; no mathematical content, rate, or guarantee is withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 ($\ell=8$) the listed values $1$ and $-1$ each occur twice, so there are only 6 distinct modulus-1 roots, not $\ell=8$, and since each listed value enters $\sigma(G)$ once and $\sigma(R)^{-1}$ once, the values $1$ and $-1$ are roots of $a(z)$ of multiplicity 4, not 2. This contradicts the quoted verification claim and violates the standing assumptions of Section 2.2 beyond the complex-entry deviation the paper explicitly acknowledges.

failure_location.quote: One can easily verify that both $G$ and $R$ have $\ell$ eigenvalues on the unit circle and $m-\ell$ eigenvalues inside the unit circle. Moreover, $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ are eigenvalues of $A(z)$ of multiplicity 2.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the repeated values in Case 3 by distinct modulus-1 values, or explicitly extend the assumptions of Section 2.2 to repeated unit-modulus roots and note that the analysis carries over.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's own test case (Case 3 of Table tab:example3mu) is not covered by the assumptions under which the theory and guarantees are stated; the claimed verification for that case is false as written (the reported experiments themselves are unaffected as empirical evidence).
issues.title: Example 3, Case 3 violates the paper's own distinctness/multiplicity assumptions
